title: Why CIOs need a business integration strategy for 2027
summary: Your AI strategy may have an integration problem. See why connecting the information across your ERP environment and business ecosystem should be a CIO priority.
body_markdown:
AI ambitions are moving faster than many organizations’ ability to connect the data behind them. For CIOs planning for 2027, that makes business integration strategy much more than an IT architecture decision. It is becoming essential to how the business prepares for AI, automation, and growth. The question is no longer simply where AI could add value.


Years of ERP customization, point-to-point integrations, cloud adoption, acquisitions, and evolving customer and supplier requirements have left many organizations with fragmented technology environments. Critical information is often spread across[ERP systems](https://www.opentext.com/what-is/erp-integration) , cloud applications, trading partner networks, data repositories, and manual processes.


When information cannot move reliably across a business, CIOs face a data problem, a visibility problem, and ultimately an AI-readiness problem. That’s why OpenText™ Business Network recommends you connect to a platform and network that adapts with you, especially as your ecosystem and technology priorities change, so you simplify .


## **Create a trusted data foundation through integrated business processes**


[AI and automation](https://www.gartner.com/doc/reprints?id=00ThR00000And4BUAR&ct=260817&st=sb&_gl=1*18tywm4*_gcl_au*MTA3ODcwMTgxMS4xNzkzODIwNDcw*_ga*ODY1NTE0NDc2LjE3NzgyNDUwMDM.*_ga_8LWPJ50ZXY*czE3OTQ1MDU5OTQkbzE0MCRnMCR0MTc5NDUwNTk5NSRqNTkkbDAkaDExMTY4NTA5NjA.) depend on reliable, accessible data. But when orders, invoices, shipments, inventory updates, supplier information, and other transactions move through disconnected systems, it becomes difficult to see what is happening across the business. That’s why CIOs need to look beyond the ERP itself and consider how the applications, customers, suppliers, logistics providers, and business processes surrounding it are integrated.


The answer isn’t necessarily more technology. It’s a simpler, more adaptable integration approach that makes it easier to manage existing connections and add new ones over time. This creates more reliable, accessible data for analytics, automation, and[AI](https://www.opentext.com/what-is/ai-for-business) .


## Unlock four benefits of modern business integration


For CIOs, the value comes down to simplifying what IT manages while getting more from the technology already in place:


- **Reduce technical debt and integration complexity** by decreasing dependence on custom integrations and scarce technical skills.


- **Extend the value of ERP and cloud investments** by connecting them to customers, suppliers, logistics providers, and other business systems.


- **Improve visibility and data reliability** so analytics, automation, and AI have better information to work with.


- **Support growth without scaling IT complexity at the same rate** as the business.


## **Adapt your integration strategy as the business scales**


Business integration isn’t a one-size-fits-all challenge. A global enterprise may need to simplify and govern a complex integration landscape, while a growing mid-sized organization may need to automate more without adding IT resources. The priorities differ, but the underlying requirement is the same: business information must move reliably across systems and trading partners.


For a large enterprise, priorities may include:


- Consolidating integration platforms and reducing technical debt


- Improving visibility and governance across global trading partner networks


- Establishing reliable, accessible data for automation and AI


For a mid-sized or smaller organization, priorities may include:


- Growing the business without increasing IT resources and complexity at the same pace


- Replacing spreadsheets, portals, and manual work with automated processes


- Getting more from existing technology while preparing for automation and AI


The scale may be different, but the fundamental need is the same: reliable, accessible information must flow across the business and its wider ecosystem.


## **Treat integration as a strategic capability**


This gives CIOs an opportunity to treat integration as a strategic capability rather than a series of separate technology projects. The objective isn’t optimization for its own sake. It’s making the business easier to connect, adapt, and scale while supporting today’s ERP, supply chain, customer, and operational needs.


As 2027 approaches, the organizations best positioned to benefit from AI may not be those experimenting with the most use cases. They may be the ones that have done the work to make their business data connected, accessible, and reliable.


**Put integration to work for what’s next** ****


A modern business integration strategy needs to connect more than applications. It needs to connect the wider business ecosystem.

This can help CIOs reduce integration complexity, automate critical business processes, improve operational visibility, and create more reliable data for analytics and AI.


Whether the priority is simplifying a complex global integration environment or helping a growing business scale without adding more IT complexity, the goal is the same: connect the business, simplify integration, and put your data to work.
